source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 7: Find |AA^t| and |A^tA|, parts (i)-(ii) (book page 60).

blocks.explanation:
\(A\) ka order \(2 \times 3\) hai, yani yeh square nahi, is liye \(A\) ka apna determinant nahi hota. Lekin \(AA^{t}\) (\(2 \times 2\)) aur \(A^{t}A\) (\(3 \times 3\)) dono square hain.
Humein dono products bana kar un ke determinants nikalne hain.
Plan: pehle \(A^{t}\), phir multiplication (row \(\times\) column), phir determinants.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(A = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\)
Humein find karna hai: \(|AA^{t}|\) aur \(|A^{t}A|\).
Tareeqa: Transpose (rows ko columns bana dena), matrix multiplication (pehle matrix ki row \(\cdot\) doosre ka column), phir determinant ke rules. Order check: \((2 \times 3)(3 \times 2) = 2 \times 2\) aur \((3 \times 2)(2 \times 3) = 3 \times 3\).

Transpose likhein
\[A^{t} = \begin{bmatrix} -3 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki row 1 ab \(A^{t}\) ka column 1 hai aur row 2 column 2. Order ulat kar \(3 \times 2\) ho gaya.

\(AA^{t}\) nikalein (\(2 \times 2\))
\[(1,1):\ 9 + 4 + 1 = 14\]
\[(1,2):\ -6 + 2 - 3 = -7\]
\[(2,1):\ -6 + 2 - 3 = -7\]
\[(2,2):\ 4 + 1 + 9 = 14\]
\[AA^{t} = \begin{bmatrix} 14 & -7 \\ -7 & 14 \end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Entry \((i, j)\) = \(A\) ki row \(i\) \(\times\) \(A^{t}\) ka column \(j\) (jo asal mein \(A\) ki row \(j\) hai). Masalan \((1,1)\): \((-3)(-3) + (2)(2) + (-1)(-1)\).
Dhyan dein: \(AA^{t}\) hamesha symmetric hota hai (\((1,2) = (2,1)\)); agar aap ke jawab mein yeh barabar na hon to multiplication dobara dekhein.

\(|AA^{t}|\)
\[|AA^{t}| = (14)(14) - (-7)(-7)\]
\[= 196 - 49 = 147\]
Kyun: \(2 \times 2\) rule: leading diagonal \(14 \times 14 = 196\), doosra diagonal \((-7)(-7) = +49\), aur dono ka farq 147. Do negative numbers ka product positive hota hai, yeh na bhoolein.

Tasdeeq
\[R_1 + R_2 = (9, 1, 10) = R_3\]
Kyun: Teesri row pehli do ka jama hai, to \(R_3 - R_1 - R_2\) zero row ban jati hai aur determinant zero hona hi chahiye. Asal wajah: \(A^{t}A\) sirf do numbers wale columns se bana hai, is liye us ka \(3 \times 3\) determinant zero hi aata hai. Yaad rakhein: \(|AA^{t}|\) aur \(|A^{t}A|\) aksar barabar nahi hote jab \(A\) square na ho.

blocks.explanation:
Ab \(A\) ka order \(3 \times 2\) hai: is liye \(AA^{t}\) \(3 \times 3\) aur \(A^{t}A\) \(2 \times 2\) banega (part (i) ka ulta).
Plan: \(A^{t}\) likhein, dono products banayein, determinants nikalein.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 2 \\ 1 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\)
Humein find karna hai: \(|AA^{t}|\) aur \(|A^{t}A|\).
Tareeqa: Transpose, multiplication, phir determinants. Order: \((3 \times 2)(2 \times 3) = 3 \times 3\) aur \((2 \times 3)(3 \times 2) = 2 \times 2\).

Transpose likhein
\[A^{t} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & 3 \end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(A\) ke columns ab \(A^{t}\) ki rows hain: pehla column \((3, 2, 1)\) pehli row ban gaya aur doosra column \((1, 2, 3)\) doosri row. Order \(3 \times 2\) se \(2 \times 3\) ho gaya.

\(A^{t}A\) nikalein (\(2 \times 2\))
\[A^{t}A = \begin{bmatrix} 9+4+1 & 3+4+3 \\ 3+4+3 & 1+4+9 \end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix} 14 & 10 \\ 10 & 14 \end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Entry \((i, j)\) = \(A\) ka column \(i\) \(\cdot\) column \(j\). Columns hain \((3, 2, 1)\) aur \((1, 2, 3)\).

Tasdeeq
\[R_1 + R_3 = (16, 16, 16) = 2R_2\]
Kyun: \(AA^{t}\) mein \(R_1 + R_3 - 2R_2\) zero row hai, is liye \(|AA^{t}| = 0\) bilkul sahi hai. Dhyan dein: is baar bara (\(3 \times 3\)) product zero aaya aur chhota (\(2 \times 2\)) non-zero; part (i) mein bhi yahi hua tha.
